name: Glean
h1: Glean ARR: $300M+ After Tripling in 15 Months.
intro: Glean, the enterprise AI search and work assistant, disclosed surpassing $300 million in annualized revenue in May 2026 — roughly tripling from $100M in 15 months, up about 89% year over year. Every publicly reported revenue, funding and valuation number is collected below, each traced back to a source.

modelTitle: How a Context Graph Justifies Enterprise Pricing.
modelParagraphs: Glean sells enterprise agreements priced on seats and usage of its work AI platform. Its defensibility claim is the context graph: permission-aware connections across every company app that make answers usable where generic chatbots hallucinate. That infrastructure-first position lets Glean price above point solutions and expand from search into agents that act on company knowledge.

The company reports that its win rate increases with deal complexity — 66% on simpler tasks versus 73% on complex, multi-step ones — and that customers consolidating AI tooling cut inference costs by roughly 30%. The competitive frame is increasingly Microsoft, with Glean arguing that cross-app context beats the incumbent's single-suite view.
revenueMix: Per-seat pricing on the work AI platform, sold top-down to CIOs.
Agent and assistant consumption across connected company apps.
Customers folding point tools into Glean, cutting inference costs ~30%.

faqs.a: Glean disclosed surpassing $300 million in annualized revenue on May 28, 2026 — up about 89% year over year and roughly triple the $100M it disclosed in February 2025. That implies around $25 million of monthly recurring revenue.

faqs.q: How Fast Did Glean Triple Its ARR?
faqs.a: Fifteen months, from $100M (February 2025) to $300M+ (May 2026), passing $200M roughly five months before the latest disclosure.
A $150 million Series F in June 2025 valued Glean at $7.2 billion, up from $4.6 billion at its $260 million Series E in September 2024 and $1.03 billion in February 2024.

Enterprise seat and usage agreements on its work AI platform. Its pitch is the permission-aware context graph across every company app, which it says drives rising win rates on complex deals and ~30% inference-cost savings for customers consolidating AI tools.

Increasingly Microsoft in enterprise AI search, along with point-solution chatbots. Glean argues its cross-app, permission-aware context beats single-suite assistants — and reports winning 73% of complex, multi-step deals.
